newsitem.title: USA: Yahoo! in electronic commerce deal with Visa.
newsitem.headline: Yahoo! in electronic commerce deal with Visa.

text.p: Internet company Yahoo! Inc. said Tuesday it formed a new global electronic commerce alliance with Visa International and restated its second-quarter results to reflect a related one-time non-cash charge.

Under the agreement, Yahoo! and the credit card organisation will collaborate on several electronic commerce initiatives, including shopping guides, a co-branded Yahoo! Visa card and joint promotions of the Yahoo! and Visa brands.
Visa International and Yahoo! said they entered into the alliance to "aggressively extend their commerce-related activities on the Internet."
Yahoo! operates one of the most popular search engines on the World Wide Web, a searchable catalogue that allows computer users to find things on the vast Internet.

The Santa Clara, Calif-based company said it had issued 466,321 shares of Yahoo! common stock to the Visa Group and took a one-time, non-cash pre-tax charge of $21,245,000 in its second quarter ending June 30.

As a result, Yahoo! said it was restating its second-quarter results to show a net loss of $20.5 million, or 74 cents a share, compared with a net loss of $1.3 million, or 5 cents a share in the same year-ago quarter.
Excluding the one-time, non-cash charge, net income for the second quarter of 1997 was $610,000, or 2 cents a share, as previously reported July 9.
Yahoo! also said Tuesday its board had approved a three-for-two stock split.
Yahoo! Chief Executive Tim Koogle said the agreement will give the comppany flexibility to pursue electronic commerce while retaining 100 percent of the financial benefit for Yahoo! shareholders.
The announcement was made after the close of trading. Yahoo's stock rose 69 cents to $48.25 on Nasdaq.
